When designing a Wi-Fi-based WLAN to support voice in a large office, which design element is of the highest concern for performance?
Roaming performance depends on how quickly a client can move between APs and complete reassociation. Delays or interruptions are especially noticeable to voice applications.
What is the minimum PoE budget required to power 6 APs using IEEE 802.3at with no additional details provided?
IEEE 802.3at can supply up to 30 W per powered device at the PSE. Using the maximum per-AP budget, 6 × 30 W = 180 W.
In high-density environments like stadiums or convention centers, what additional factor must be considered that can attenuate Wi-Fi signals during events?
People absorb and scatter RF energy. A dense crowd can change propagation and reduce received signal levels compared with an empty venue.
Which document outlines the objectives, scope, and key stakeholders, serving as the official authorization to begin a WLAN design and deployment project?
A project charter formally authorizes the work and records its objectives, scope, stakeholders, and high-level responsibilities.
When conducting information gathering for a WLAN design, which document ensures your customer's proprietary information remains confidential and protected from unauthorized disclosure?
A nondisclosure agreement establishes a confidentiality obligation and limits how the customer's proprietary information may be shared.
In WLAN location-based services, which metric, despite being commonly used, offers the lowest accuracy when determining device positions?
RSSI estimates distance indirectly from received power. Reflections, multipath, orientation, and client radio differences make it the least accurate of the listed location metrics.
Your customer uses PSK authentication but needs a more secure, certificate-based solution requiring certificates on both the client and server. Which EAP method is the most appropriate?
EAP-TLS uses mutual certificate authentication: both the authentication server and the client prove their identity with certificates.
When designing a wireless bridge to connect two offices 13 kilometers (approximately 8 miles) apart, which factor must the Wireless Engineer consider to account for Fresnel Zone clearance?
Earth curvature raises the terrain-equivalent path over long distances. The link design must include this Earth bulge when calculating antenna height and Fresnel-zone clearance.
While conducting a site survey in a heavy machinery repair facility, what essential gear should you use for safety in this challenging environment?
Site-survey and installation work must follow the facility's access rules and use appropriate personal protective equipment for the hazards present.

A North American business traveler connects to a hotel's 2.4 GHz SSID in Europe and notices low RSSI from an AP in the room, but experiences no issues with RSSI in the lobby. What is the most likely reason for the low RSSI in the room?
The AP in the room is using ZigBee instead of Wi-Fi
The AP in the room is transmitting on channel 13 and the traveler associated to an AP on channels 1 through 11 in the lobby
The switchport that the AP is connected to is only capable of transmitting at 10 Mbps
The AP in the room is using Bluetooth instead of Wi-Fi
Channel 13 is permitted in many European regulatory domains but is not available to some North American client configurations. Region settings can therefore prevent discovery.

A museum requires its wireless access points to be discreetly integrated into the environment without sacrificing performance. Which design choice best meets this requirement while maintaining optimal functionality?
Lock the AP inside of a metal box
Place the APs in between walls and I-beams
Use an 802.11b AP, so it looks old enough to be in a museum
Use a plastic cover that could blend in with the environment
A purpose-designed nonmetallic cover can improve appearance while avoiding the severe RF attenuation caused by metal enclosures; manufacturer guidance and warranty terms still apply.

An engineering firm upgraded from nine 802.11n APs to nine 802.11ac APs, retaining the same channel and power configuration. Despite this, throughput remains unchanged. What is the most likely reason for the lack of improvement?
APs are transmitting at a low transmit power
APs are mounted on the wall
The APs are still using the 5 GHz lower band
A faster AP cannot deliver the newer PHY's benefits to legacy clients that lack the corresponding radio capabilities.

During a public Wi-Fi session with 10 other users, you run a ping sweep but cannot detect any devices on your subnet. What feature is likely enabled on the WLAN infrastructure to prevent local communication between clients?
Client isolation prevents wireless stations on the same WLAN from communicating directly with one another, even though they share the SSID or subnet.
While implementing 802.11ax APs in the 6 GHz band, a consultant recommends using WPA2- Personal for VoIP support. Why is this approach technically inappropriate?
Because WPA2-Personal causes slower roams than WPA2-Enterprise
Because 802.11ax does not support WPA2-Personal in any band
Because 6 GHz WLANs cannot use WPA2-Personal
Because VoIP requires Opportunistic Wireless Encryption (OWE)
The 6 GHz band does not permit WPA2-Personal. Wi-Fi 6E/6 GHz networks must use the security mechanisms allowed for that band, such as WPA3 or Enhanced Open where applicable.
While planning for a VoWLAN deployment requiring 25 dB SNR, you measure the noise floor at -88 dBm. What is the minimum RSSI needed to meet the system's performance requirements?
Required RSSI = noise floor + required SNR. −88 dBm + 25 dB = −63 dBm.
When deploying an Enterprise-class VoWLAN infrastructure, which Access Category (AC) must be used to prioritize voice packets and ensure optimal performance?
AC_VO is the WMM voice access category. It receives the most favorable contention parameters to reduce delay for latency-sensitive voice packets.
When using a WLAN design tool with propagation modeling capabilities, what critical step must be performed before adding APs, antennas, and attenuation factors like walls?
Set the transmit power for all APs
Nothing; just begin by adding APs, antenna and attenuators
Calibrate the floor plan to increase accuracy
A predictive model needs a correctly scaled and calibrated floor plan so distances, wall locations, and attenuation are represented accurately.

Your customer's 802.11n laptops cannot detect the SSID in the 5 GHz band in a conference room, but your 802.11ac laptop connects without issue. What is the most likely explanation for this discrepancy?
The AP is configured to use channel 36
The customer laptop does not support OFDM
Some legacy 5 GHz client radios do not support channel 144. If the AP uses that channel, those clients may not discover the SSID.
When designing a static channel plan for an office using voice devices near an airport, which range of channels may be avoided to avoid channel switching when implemented in this environment?
Channels 116–124 are DFS channels in the 5 GHz band. Radar detection can force channel changes, which may disrupt real-time voice clients.
Which vertically polarized antenna is best suited for a WLAN infrastructure with access points mounted on a ceiling over 6 meters high, where all client stations operate from the floor level?

A low-gain dipole has a broad, near-omnidirectional azimuth pattern and a relatively broad vertical pattern, helping reach floor-level clients from a high ceiling without concentrating energy too narrowly.

When using a predictive design tool, you have selected access points (APs) with an antenna gain of 3 dBi and set the transmit power to 25 mW. What is the EIRP (Effective Isotropic Radiated Power) of the APs in this design?
Convert 25 mW to approximately 14 dBm, then add 3 dBi antenna gain: EIRP is approximately 17 dBm, assuming no feed-line loss.

Your customer has selected switches that support 802.3bz MultiGig interfaces and 4x4:4 802.11ac Wave 2 APs with dual-5GHz capabilities. The APs have one MultiGig interface, and some cable runs will exceed 180.5 feet (55 meters). To support MultiGig speeds, which is the best cabling option?
The cabling choice must support the required Ethernet rate over the actual channel length. Use the cable category and distance limits specified for the target PHY.

When conducting a site survey for a possible WLAN redesign, you use two Wi-Fi USB adapters for RSSI data collection and two USB spectrum analysis adapters for RF spectrum data. Since your laptop lacks enough USB ports, you connect them via a 4-port powered USB 3.0 hub. What issue could the use of USB 3.0 cause that might impact your site survey?
It does not give you enough bandwidth to collect data coming from all of the adapters
No USB 3.0 hub provides enough power for all the adapters
It generates noise in the 2.4 GHz band, giving you a false perception of the noise floor
It generates noise in the 5 GHz band, giving you a false perception of the noise floor
USB 3.0 devices and cables can radiate interference in the 2.4 GHz band. That noise can raise the apparent noise floor and make survey measurements misleading.
What is the most cost-effective way to accurately measure the height of a ceiling when the use of a ladder is not permitted?
Estimate the height based on known object sizes
Gather measurements from other objects and do the math
Rent a lift-cart to lift you up to the ceiling
Use a laser measure to measure the distance from the floor to the ceiling
A laser distance meter measures floor-to-ceiling distance directly without requiring ladder access.

You conducted a site survey using two USB Wi-Fi adapters with a special driver designed for the site survey software. After deployment, the client devices show lower RSSI values compared to the results from your survey. What is the most likely reason for this discrepancy?
USB Wi-Fi adapters designed for site surveys may have better sensitivity than regular Wi-Fi cards installed in client devices
The transmit power on the APs is higher than needed
Regular Wi-Fi cards installed in client devices do not support the same protocols as survey adapters
All USB Wi-Fi adapters have a greater sensitivity than internal Wi-Fi adapters
Survey adapters can have different antenna characteristics and receive sensitivity than production client devices, so survey RSSI may not match what end users experience.
When performing an active site survey in an existing WLAN infrastructure, in addition to gathering throughput data, what other important function are you typically testing simultaneously?
Roaming performance depends on how quickly a client can move between APs and complete reassociation. Delays or interruptions are especially noticeable to voice applications.
Why should band steering algorithms allow stations to connect to the 2.4 GHz band after ignoring a certain number of Probe Requests?
Because some clients are persistent clients that will not move to the 5 GHz band
Because the AP will experience a buffer overflow if they do not eventually respond with a Probe Response
Band steering is a preference mechanism, not a guarantee. The AP should eventually admit persistent or legacy clients that will not move to 5 GHz.

After designing a WLAN infrastructure using predictive design software, what is the best way to validate the predictive design in the physical space before deployment, assuming time and budget allow for it?
Deploy all of the APs as they're shown in the predictive design and perform an active site survey
Deploy all of the APs as they're shown in the predictive design and perform a passive site survey
Use a client device positioned where the APs will be installed and measure the signal from the client device
Perform an AP-on-a-Stick survey using AP locations based upon the predictive design to confirm each AP's placement
An AP-on-a-Stick survey temporarily places an AP at proposed locations and measures real propagation, validating or refining the predictive model before full deployment.

Your customer requires a security solution where client credentials are used, not a Protected Access Credential (PAC), and the authentication server must have a certificate with optional client certificate use. Which EAP (Extensible Authentication Protocol) method is the best fit for these requirements?
EAP-TTLS authenticates the server with a certificate and protects the client's credentials inside a TLS tunnel; unlike EAP-TLS, it does not require a client certificate.
Your customer requires fast and secure roaming. Which two types of roaming are specified in 802.11 Fast Transition (FT) that will help meet this goal?
802.11r Fast BSS Transition supports two exchange paths: over-the-air directly with the target AP, or over-the-DS through the distribution system.
Which advantage provided by 802.11n and 802.11ac is not usable in 1x1:1 low-end client devices?
MRC combines signals from multiple receive chains to improve the effective received signal and SNR; a 1x1 client cannot benefit from multiple receive chains.
When deploying access points (APs) outdoors, which additional component needs to be used that is typically not required in most indoor office deployments?
Outdoor APs may need NEMA-rated enclosures to protect the equipment from weather, dust, and other environmental exposure when the AP itself is not rated for those conditions.
Which document provided to your customer should include all devices and parts that will be used during the deployment of their WLAN infrastructure?
A bill of materials lists the equipment, components, quantities, and parts required for the deployment.
What limitation exists when WMM is not enabled on an 802.11 WLAN?
The maximum channel-width will be 20 MHz
Only two ACs will be available
WMM is the Wi-Fi Alliance implementation of 802.11e QoS. Without WMM, the WLAN cannot provide the standardized wireless traffic-priority queues.
When designing for OFDMA, why might the same channel bandwidth result in greater efficiency than that available in 802.11n and 802.11ac?
The design will use MU-MIMO, which is not available in either 802.11n or 802.11ac.
The design will use transmit beamforming, which is not available in either 802.11n or 802.11ac.
The design will use RUs that allow for transmissions to multiple client devices concurrently without the use of MU-MIMO.
The clients will use UL MU-MIMO coupled with DSSS, which was not available in 802.11n or 802.11ac.
OFDMA divides a channel into resource units so an AP can schedule transmissions to multiple clients concurrently, improving airtime efficiency.
What service must be implemented on your customer's network to authenticate users against an LDAP database before granting access to the WLAN infrastructure?
RADIUS provides centralized AAA between the WLAN authenticator and the authentication service; it can validate users against a connected identity store such as LDAP.
What is the best method of gathering attenuation measurements from wall materials?

After measuring the RSSI in free space 5 meters (16.5 feet) apart, put an AP 4 meters (13 feet) away from the wall on one side and your measuring device 1 meter (3.2 feet) away from the wall minus the width of the wall. Take measurements and compare the difference.
Use the pre-built attenuation values in the predictive design tools as they are more accurate than free-space metrics gathered with commercial devices.

After measuring the RSSI in free space 1 meter (3 feet) apart, put an AP 0.32 meters (1 feet) away from the wall on one side and your measuring device 0.67 meters (2 feet) away from the wall on the other side. Take measurements and compare the difference.
Look on the Internet for attenuation values for each one of the materials that might attenuate the Wi-Fi signal using the material providers' websites.
Measure a free-space baseline at a controlled distance, then repeat with the material in the path. The difference estimates that material's attenuation.
Which type of authentication and encryption method is mandatory for Voice Enterprise certified devices as specified by the Wi-Fi Alliance?
Wi-Fi Alliance Voice Enterprise certification requires enterprise authentication with AES-based encryption, providing per-user authentication and strong link protection.
Which document provides detailed instructions for installation technicians on how to properly mount and configure access points (APs)?
A physical installation guide translates the RF design into actionable mounting locations, methods, cabling, and configuration instructions for installers.

In addition to a copy of your design, which tools should you provide to ensure the installation team correctly deploys access points (APs) in the specified locations within a multi-floor indoor design?
RF spectrum analyzer and packet capturing software
A ladder provides safe access to the specified mounting locations, and a pen can be used to mark the installation points shown in the design.
